task: Add a tool-agnostic one-line Analytics health field (text + --json) to `codemie proxy status`, backed by spool/auth-marker reads and an additive stale-credentials field on the daemon `/health` reply, and restyle `codemie proxy analytics status` (all connectors) to the proxy-status style with a shared Delivery section.

key_reasoning.reason: Touches the proxy status command, both analytics status collect/format renderers (Claude and Copilot) plus hints, a new shared spool delivery-health collector over otlp-spool session-status/spool-state, the analytics auth marker reader, and the SSO proxy /health handler with the daemon auth-state flag — 4+ components across CLI, proxy plugin and daemon.

No precedent for a CLI command reading the OTLP spool; the closest patterns (collect/format split, never-throwing health result, markerAppliesToProfile) cover rendering and auth-marker reads but not the cross-process /health contract change (consumed by daemon-manager identity check) or spool-scan cost against the 1.5s shallow status budget. Auth-blocked backlog leaves no on-disk record, so the unhealthy rules depend on the in-memory flag being surfaced correctly. Exact-string tests on both outputs will break on restyle.

About 8-10 source/test files modified (proxy index, analytics-status, analytics-command, analytics-hints, sso.proxy /health, auth-state, possibly health-check/daemon-manager, plus index/analytics-status/analytics-advice/analytics-command/daemon-status-contract tests) and 1-2 new modules (shared delivery-health collector + test), across src/cli/commands/proxy, src/providers/plugins/sso/proxy and docs (README, COMMANDS.md, tips.json).

Requirements are explicit: visibility rule, four unhealthy conditions with reasons and tips, JSON shape addition, Delivery section contents and explicit exclusions (no new disk files, no session-sync, no trend). Only minor details (exact labels for hold reasons, wording) remain. Calibration: bundled M example epmcdme-10203 (total 15) has a less clear spec but lower risk/file count; this task sits above it in the M band, consistent with 18.
